notes.title: Cerebral Puzzle Showcase Stream!
notes.notes: We're so excited to be part of the Cerebral Puzzle Showcase! Watch our Community Director Marty completely forget how puzzles work and also completely forget anything she ever thought she learned from her first playthrough of GNOG from KO_OP, available fo 25% off from May 19-23!

notes.title: Patch – v1.0.7
notes.notes:
[h1]Accessibility[/h1]
[list]
[*] Support for eye-gaze controllers. Working with charity [url=https://www.specialeffect.org.uk/]SpecialEffect[/url], we’ve provided a new launch option where certain widgets can be controlled more easily with assistive mouse devices. Instead of clicking and holding the mouse to move an object, you only need to click the mouse once to grab something, then click again to release it. To play in this mode, choose “Play with mouse accessibility support,” or launch the game with the command-line argument “--eyegaze”. If you play GNOG with assistive devices, we’d love to hear your feedback! Thanks again to SpecialEffect for their patience and continued help in making this feature possible.
[/list]

[h1]Bug fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed: removed some conflicting animations in CANDY
[*] Fixed: ignore mouse input while in VR.
[/list]

notes.title: Melon-twisting puzzler Gnog is free on the Epic Games Store
notes.notes:
“Gnog is absolutely spellbinding and charming in its daft, joyful silliness,” our former John (RPS in peace) said in his Gnog review when it finally came out last year. A big fan of twiddling and twisting and tugging heads to see the secrets they hold, that one. And in the game. Gnog hands us playful puzzleheads to open up, look inside, fiddle with, and eventually solve. The mucking-about is just as important as the solving, see. If you missed Gnog, hey, it’s now the latest freebie on the Epic Games Store.

notes.title: Halloween 2018 Special: Some lovely games!
notes.notes:
Video games, you may have noticed, are often a little bit horrid. All sorts of naughtiness, and a distinct lack of people just being kind to one another. What are we like?! But fortunately there are games that make an exception to the potty-mouthed meanies that dominate, and today I celebrate them and their cuteness with a collection of lovely screenshots.

notes.title: How cutting off heads got GNOG finished
notes.notes:
This is The Mechanic, where Alex Wiltshire invites developers to discuss the difficult journeys they ve taken to make their games. This time, GNOG [official site].

Samuel Boucher hadn t really made a game before he started to make GNOG. He was an artist and graphic designer, and though he d art directed an interactive jigsaw puzzle game for kids, that was pretty much the limit of his experience. So, really, you can say the trouble with GNOG started when he decided to post some illustrations of a game idea he had to a local indie developer forum. His art talents were quite enough to attract the interest of indie studio KO-OP, and so started three years of trying to figure out how to actually make it. It was a really big mess, Boucher tells me. (more…)

notes.title: Patch – v1.0.5
notes.notes:
[h1]Features[/h1]
[list]
[*] VR: Clicking the thumbpad/stick in the Level Select will now rotate through the level carousel
[*] [b]Experimental[/b]: Support for more Windows MR controllers. Please report ongoing issues.
[/list]

[h1]Bug fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed: single-frame graphical hiccups entering Level Select
[*] Fixed: Pause, Title, & Level select UI’s don’t reflect SFX volume settings
[*] Fixed: EATER front doors could be opened out of sequence
[*] Fixed: In VR, grabbing/releasing with one wand would impact the state of the other wand, if the latter was present and hovering over a widget
[/list]

notes.title: Patch – v1.0.4
notes.notes:
[h1]Features[/h1]
[list]
[*] Controlling wheels/dials with an input other than a joystick is now a left-right motion, rather than the circular motion which was causing some difficulty
[*] Support for second Vive wand
[*] [b]Experimental[/b]: Support for more headsets, including: Vive Pro, Lenovo Explorer, Acer AH100, and HP & Samsung Windows Mixed Reality Headsets. Please report ongoing issues.
[/list]

[h1]Bug fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed: CANDY gumball win-sequence could be fired multiple times
[*] Fixed: Could tap nose before final burglar animation was finished in HOM-3
[*] Fixed: Rear handle in INTRO could be grabbed in VR while facing the front of the gnoggin
[*] Fixed: Experiment rings in LAB-O not snapping to correct final value
[*] Fixed: “Launch VR” falling back to flat mode when HMD is not mounted
[*] Fixed: hovering over separate items with both VR wands would cause audio/control conflicts
[/list]

notes.title: Gnog s pretty puzzleheads opening up in November
notes.notes: The pretty puzzleheads of Gnog will finally come to PC some time in November. Ko_op’s Gnog traps us inside giant monstrous heads, where I suppose our objective is to escape but that seems a lot less fun than messing about.
